## 3-Pillar System

| Pillar | Name | Components | Objective |
|--------|------|------------|-----------|
| **1st** | State pension | AVS · IAI · PC | Minimum subsistence |
| **2nd** | Occupational pension | LPP · LAA | Maintaining standard of living |
| **3rd** | Private pension | 3a (linked) · 3b (free) | Supplementary needs |

::: {.callout-note title="Key figure"}
Elderly >65 years threatened by poverty : **51 % in 1979 → ~15–20 % today**
:::

---

## Simple Returns

### Fundamental Formulas

**1 period :**

$$R_1(t) = \frac{P(t)}{P(t-1)} - 1 \qquad \Leftrightarrow \qquad 1 + R_1(t) = \frac{P(t)}{P(t-1)}$$

**$n$ periods — multiplicative compounding :**

$$1 + R_n(t) = \prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\bigl(1 + R_1(t-i)\bigr)$$

**Portfolio ($n$ assets, $\sum\alpha_i = 1$) :**

$$R_p = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \alpha_i R_i$$

### Numerical Example

| Time | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|------|---|---|---|---|
| Price | 10 | 12 | 14 | 16 |
| $R_1$ | — | 20% | 16,7% | 14,3% |

- **Sum** : $20\% + 16.7\% + 14.3\% = 50.9\%$ ❌
- **Product** : $(1.20)(1.167)(1.143) - 1 = 60\%$ ✅

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap — Never sum simple returns"}
Multi-period simple returns **compound** (product), they do **not sum**.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap — Asymmetry"}
$+20\%$ then $-20\%$ **≠** back to starting point. Rise from 50 → 60 (+20%), return : 60 → 50 (−16,7%).
:::

---

## Annualisation

| Base | Formula |
|------|---------|
| Monthly → Annual | $R_a = (1 + R_m)^{12} - 1$ |
| Daily → Annual | $R_a = (1 + R_d)^{256} - 1$ |

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap — Do not simply multiply"}
$R_a \neq 12 \times R_m$ · Always use compounding · Convention : 250 / 256 / 300 days depending on markets.
:::

## Time Value of Money

### Discrete vs Continuous Compounding

| Frequency | Formula | Value (PV=1000, R=10%, n=1) |
|-----------|---------|------------------------------|
| Annual | $PV(1+R)^n$ | 1 100,0 CHF |
| Quarterly | $PV(1+R/4)^{4n}$ | 1 103,8 CHF |
| Daily | $PV(1+R/365)^{365n}$ | 1 105,2 CHF |
| **Continuous** | $PV \cdot e^{Rn}$ | **1 105,2 CHF** |

### Simple rate ↔ continuous rate relation

$$r = \ln(1+R) \quad \Longrightarrow \quad r < R$$

$$R = e^r - 1$$

**Example :** $R = 10\%$ → $r = \ln(1.10) = 9.53\%$

::: {.callout-note title="Key takeaway"}
Continuous compounding = **theoretical** tool (exponential more convenient analytically), not realistic in practice.
:::

---

## Continuous / Logarithmic Returns

### Formula

$$r(t) = \ln\!\left(\frac{P_t}{P_{t-1}}\right) = \ln P_t - \ln P_{t-1}$$

### Simple vs logarithmic comparison

| Property | Simple returns | Log returns |
|----------|----------------|-------------|
| Multi-period | **Product** $\prod(1+R_i)$ | **Sum** $\sum r_i$ |
| Portfolio | $R_p = \sum\alpha_i R_i$ ✅ | $r_p \neq \sum\alpha_i r_i$ ⚠️ |
| Symmetry | ❌ Asymmetric | ✅ Symmetric |
| Range | $]-1,+\infty[$ | $]-\infty,+\infty[$ |

::: {.callout-important title="Temporal additivity of log-returns"}
$r_n(t) = \displaystyle\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} r_1(t-i)$ — valid **only** for temporal aggregation, **not** for portfolios.
:::

## Bookkeeping

### NAV formula with foreign asset

$$\text{NAV (CHF)} = \text{position} \times \text{price (USD)} \times \text{USDCHF} + \text{Cash (CHF)}$$

### Summary of 4 cases

| Case | Fixed FX ? | Hedged ? | P&L | Risks exposed |
|------|-----------|----------|-----|---------------|
| CHF → CHF asset | — | — | +105 CHF | Equity only |
| CHF → USD asset, fixed FX | ✅ | ❌ | +9 CHF | Equity only |
| CHF → USD asset, variable FX | ❌ | ❌ | −0,8 CHF | Equity **+** FX |
| CHF → USD asset, variable FX | ❌ | ✅ | +7,6 CHF | Equity only (hedge cost = 2,4 CHF) |

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap — Currency risk"}
Even if the asset price in USD returns to its initial level, the **NAV in CHF can be lower** if the dollar depreciated in the meantime.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="FX Hedging"}
- **Principle** : short USD position to neutralise FX risk
- **Advantage** : reduces NAV volatility
- **Cost** : interest rate differential between the two currencies
:::

## Summary of key formulas

| Concept | Formula |
|---------|---------|
| Simple return 1 period | $R_1(t) = P(t)/P(t-1) - 1$ |
| Simple return $n$ periods | $1 + R_n = \prod(1+R_i)$ |
| Portfolio return | $R_p = \sum\alpha_i R_i$ |
| Annualisation (monthly) | $R_a = (1+R_m)^{12} - 1$ |
| Discrete compounding | $FV = PV(1+R)^n$ |
| Continuous compounding | $FV = PV \cdot e^{Rn}$ |
| Continuous ↔ simple rate | $r = \ln(1+R)$ |
| Log-return 1 period | $r(t) = \ln(P_t/P_{t-1})$ |
| Log-return $n$ periods | $r_n(t) = \sum r_i(t)$ |
